devanagari: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः। तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि।
iast: oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ | tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi |
english: Om. We meditate on the divine Sun's glorious light;
may it awaken our minds.

source: Hymn to Mitra (Rigveda 3.59.6, in a variant reading)
english: The glory of Mitra, the god who upholds all peoples,
is true, all-winning, and of the brightest renown.
note: The chant clearly has "shravo ... sanasim ... satyam", where the Rigveda has "avo ... sanasi ... dyumnam". We believe this is the Yajurveda reading, but have not yet confirmed its source. The same verse is chanted again at 0:53:17 and 1:36:13.

source: Hymn to Mitra (Rigveda 3.59.1, in a variant reading), first half
english: Mitra, knowing all, sets the peoples in order;
Mitra holds up the earth and the sky.
note: Only the first half is clearly identifiable. The chant has "prajanan" (knowing) where the Rigveda has "bruvanah" (speaking), apparently the same variant tradition as the verse above; the line is heard again at 1:36:27.

devanagari: बुद्धं शरणं गच्छामि। धम्मं शरणं गच्छामि।
iast: buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi | dhammaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi |
english: I take refuge in the Buddha. I take refuge in the Dharma.
I take refuge in the Sangha.
note: Buddhist chanting breaks in on the Vedic worship.

devanagari: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः। तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि।
iast: oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ | tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi |
english: Om. We meditate on the divine Sun's glorious light;
may it awaken our minds.
note: The Vedic chant resumes over the Buddhist one.

devanagari: मधु वाता ऋतायते मधु क्षरन्ति सिन्धवः।
iast: madhu vātā ṛtāyate madhu kṣaranti sindhavaḥ |
english: The winds blow honey-sweet for the righteous,
the rivers run sweet; may the plants be sweet for us.

devanagari: मधु वाता ऋतायते मधु क्षरन्ति सिन्धवः।
iast: madhu vātā ṛtāyate madhu kṣaranti sindhavaḥ |
english: The winds blow honey-sweet for the righteous,
the rivers run sweet; may the plants be sweet for us.
Sweet be the night and the dawns, sweet the earth's air;
sweet be Heaven, our father.
note: Heavily garbled in recognition; identified because these verses conventionally follow 1.90.6. Needs a careful listen.

english: Sweet be the trees to us, and sweet the sun;
sweet be the cows to us.
note: As above; the word "suryah" is audible.

english: ...holding the life-breath at the crown of the head,
steadfast in the discipline of yoga,
note: Timing within this passage is approximate until word-level timings are checked.

english: uttering Om, the one syllable that is Brahman,
and remembering Me,
note: Only fragments are audible; identified from 8.12 above.

english: whoever departs, leaving the body,
reaches the highest goal.
note: Only fragments are audible; identified from 8.12 above.

source: Vedasara Shiva Stava (attributed to Shankara), verse beginning "paratmanam ekam"
english: The supreme Self, the One, the first seed of the world,
free of desire, formless, known through Om.
Let my breath return to the deathless wind,
and this body end in ashes.
note: Only "amrtam athedam bhasmantam" is clearly audible. The older subtitles place a related line near 0:09:31, so the start time needs checking.

devanagari: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः। तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि।
iast: oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ | tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi |
english: Om. We meditate on the divine Sun's glorious light;
may it awaken our minds.
note: Only the end of the mantra is audible; it probably begins earlier.

speaker: Shankara
source: Ritual formula of the young student begging alms
english: Revered lady, give me alms.

speaker: Shankara
source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship
english: As rain fallen from the sky makes its way to the sea,
so worship of every god goes on to Keshava.

source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship (first half, repeated)
english: As rain fallen from the sky makes its way to the sea...
note: Sung with "sagaram pratigacchati", as heard; the usual text reads "yatha gacchati sagaram".

source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship
english: As rain fallen from the sky
makes its way to the sea,
note: Chanted at Shivaguru's funeral. Sung with "sagaram pratigacchati", as heard; the usual text reads "yatha gacchati sagaram".

source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship
english: so worship of every god
goes on to Keshava.

source: Gayatri mantra, Rigveda 3.62.10, offered into the fire
devanagari: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः। तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि।
iast: oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ | tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi |
english: Om. We meditate on the divine Sun's glorious light;
may it awaken our minds. Svaha!

source: Gayatri mantra, Rigveda 3.62.10, offered into the fire
devanagari: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः। तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि।
iast: oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ | tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi |
english: Om. We meditate on the divine Sun's glorious light;
may it awaken our minds.
Two birds, close companions,
cling to the same tree.
One of them eats the sweet fruit;
the other, not eating, simply looks on.
The other, not eating, simply looks on.

speaker: Students
english: I bow to Parvati and Shiva, parents of the world,
joined like word and meaning, that I may grasp both.
note: Only the second half is clearly audible; the verse probably begins a little earlier.

speaker: Students
source: Kalidasa, Raghuvamsha, canto 1 (King Dilipa reaches Vasishtha's hermitage)
english: At the close of the evening rite
he saw the sage, a treasure of austerity,

speaker: Students
english: with Arundhati beside him,
like the sacred fire with Svaha at its side.
note: The audio seems to have "adhyasitam"; the standard text reads "anvasitam".

english: Fools disregard Me
when I take on a human form.
note: Quoted half in jest by a boy who feels ignored.

speaker: Shankara
source: Ritual formula of the young student begging alms
english: Revered lady, give me alms.
Fruit fallen from the wish-tree of the Veda,
sweetened by nectar from Shuka's lips:
note: Heard in the background while Shankara waits at the door.

english: drink deep of the Bhagavata, again and again,
you on earth who know its taste and are moved!

speaker: Shankara
english: Like a bee alighting on a tamala tree in bud,
it rests on Hari, whose body thrills with joy:
note: Tradition says Shankara composed this hymn to Lakshmi for a poor woman who could give him only an amalaka (gooseberry), and that golden gooseberries rained on her house.

speaker: Shankara
english: that playful sidelong glance, which holds all riches:
may the glance of the goddess of fortune bless me.

speaker: Shankara
source: Ritual formula of the young student begging alms
english: Revered lady, give me alms.

speaker: Shankara
source: Ritual formula of the young student begging alms
english: Revered lady, give me alms.

speaker: Shankara
source: Ritual formula of the young student begging alms
english: Revered lady, give me alms.
Enjoy through renunciation.
note: Quoted within a conversation about sharing food; only the quotation is given here.

english: A Brahmin guest enters a house like fire itself;
they soothe him so: bring water, O Yama!
note: Yama's household warns him that a Brahmin guest has waited unfed.

speaker: Yama
english: Three nights you have stayed in my house unfed,
O Brahmin, a guest worthy of honour.

speaker: Yama
english: My homage to you, Brahmin; may all be well with me.
In return, choose three boons.

speaker: Nachiketa
english: That my father may be calm and kind of heart,
his anger toward me gone, O Death...

speaker: Nachiketa
english: You know the fire that leads to heaven, O Death;
explain it to me, for I have faith.

speaker: Nachiketa
english: When a man has died, there is this doubt:
some say he is, and some say he is not.

speaker: Nachiketa
english: Taught by you, let me know the truth of it.
Of my boons, this is the third.

speaker: Yama
english: Nachiketa, do not question me about death.
Choose another boon.
note: The play joins phrases from two of Yama's verses.

speaker: Nachiketa
english: No other boon is equal to this one.

speaker: Yama
english: Choose sons and grandsons to live a hundred years,
cattle in plenty, elephants, gold and horses;

speaker: Yama
english: choose a vast estate on the earth,
and live yourself as many autumns as you wish.

speaker: Nachiketa
english: No one is ever satisfied by wealth.
Having seen you, we shall have wealth enough;

speaker: Nachiketa
english: we shall live as long as you hold sway.
But the boon I choose is that one alone.

speaker: Yama
english: This insight is not won by argument;
taught by another, dear one, it is truly understood.

speaker: Yama
english: You have found it, for you hold fast to truth.
May we always have a questioner like you, Nachiketa!

speaker: Shankara
source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship
english: As rain fallen from the sky makes its way to the sea,
so worship of every god goes on to Keshava.
note: Sung on the journey; only parts are clearly audible. As elsewhere in the film's singing, the first line ends "sagaram pratigacchati".

speaker: Shankara
english: Tell me who You are, so terrible in form.
I bow to You, greatest of gods: be gracious.
note: Shankara's vision of the cosmos in its terrible form. Timing within the verse is approximate.

speaker: Shankara
english: I long to know You, the Primal One,
for I do not understand what You are doing.

source: The Navkar (Namokar) Mantra, Jain, in Prakrit
devanagari: नमो अरिहंताणं। नमो सिद्धाणं। नमो आयरियाणं।
iast: namo arihaṃtāṇaṃ | namo siddhāṇaṃ | namo āyariyāṇaṃ |
english: Homage to the Arihants, to the Siddhas, to the Acharyas,
to the teachers, and to all the holy ones in the world.
note: Jain monks chanting as Shankara passes. The first three lines are clearly audible.

english: He finds a firm abode, who knows this.
He who knows the abode of the waters...
note: The same lines are chanted twice.

speaker: Vishnu
english: Established in yoga, do your work, Arjuna,
setting attachment aside.
note: Quoted by Shankara's friend Vishnu; only the quotation is given here.

source: Hymn to Mitra (Rigveda 3.59.6, in a variant reading)
devanagari: ॐ मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतः श्रवो देवस्य सानसिम्।
iast: oṃ mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ śravo devasya sānasim |
english: The glory of Mitra, the god who upholds all peoples,
is true, all-winning, and of the brightest renown.

speaker: Shankara
english: One may renounce straight from studenthood.
note: Quoted to justify renouncing the world without first becoming a householder; only the quotation is given here.

speaker: Shankara
english: You are the first of gods, the ancient Person,
the final resting place of all this world.
note: Recited to calm the flooding Narmada.

speaker: Shankara
devanagari: वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
iast: vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma
english: You are the knower and the known, the highest home;
by You, of endless forms, the world is pervaded.
What is unreal never comes to be;
what is real never ceases to be.
note: Quoted within a conversation about the body and the Self; only the quotation is given here.

english: The Self is to the south, the Self is to the north;
the Self alone is all this.
note: The chant may begin a little earlier, with "atmaivadhastat...", which is not clearly audible.

devanagari: स वा एष एवं पश्यन्नेवं मन्वान
iast: sa vā eṣa evaṃ paśyannevaṃ manvāna
english: One who sees this, who thinks this,
who knows this,
rejoicing in the Self, playing in the Self,
one with it, in its bliss, is his own sovereign.

speaker: Shankara
english: Only the clay is real.
note: Quoted in an argument with doubters; only the quotation is given here.

speaker: Shankara
english: Satyakama Jabala
once said to his mother, Jabala:

speaker: Shankara
english: "Mother, I wish to become a student of the Veda.
What is my lineage?"

speaker: Jabala
english: In my youth I wandered much, a servant girl,
and then I had you.
note: The scene is now acted out, in the Upanishad's own words.

speaker: Jabala
english: So I do not know
what lineage you are of.
note: Placed from the flow of the text and the older subtitles; the words themselves are not clearly audible here.

speaker: Jabala
english: But my name is Jabala,
and your name is Satyakama.

speaker: Satyakama
english: I do not know, sir, what my lineage is.
I asked my mother, and she answered me:

speaker: Satyakama
english: "I do not know it, child. My name is Jabala,
and yours is Satyakama."

speaker: Satyakama
english: So I am Satyakama Jabala, sir.

speaker: Gautama
english: None but a true Brahmin could speak like this.
Fetch the firewood, my boy: I will initiate you.
A Brahmin has no wealth to match this:
oneness, even-mindedness, and truth.
note: The audio has "yadekata"; the usual reading is "yathaikata".

speaker: Totaka
english: Be my refuge, Shankara, my teacher.
note: The disciple Giri sings this hymn to his teacher; Shankara then names him Totaka, after its metre.

speaker: Totaka
english: Master of the nectar-sea of all the scriptures,
treasury of the truths the Upanishads teach,

speaker: Totaka
english: I hold your spotless feet within my heart:
be my refuge, Shankara, my teacher.

speaker: Shankara
source: Bhaja Govindam (attributed to Shankara), verse 1, second half
english: When the appointed hour draws near,
no rule of grammar will save you.
note: Sung on seeing an old man still cramming rules of grammar; "dukrn karane" is one of Panini's verb-root entries.

speaker: Shankara
english: The limbs are worn, the head gone grey,
the mouth now empty of its teeth;

speaker: Shankara
english: the old man hobbles on a stick,
and still he clutches at his hopes.

speaker: Shankara
english: Worship Govinda, worship Govinda,
worship Govinda, O foolish mind!
Worship Govinda, worship Govinda,
worship Govinda, O foolish mind!
Worship Govinda, worship Govinda,
worship Govinda, O foolish mind!
Worship Govinda, worship Govinda,
worship Govinda, O foolish mind!

source: Bhaja Govindam, verse beginning "punar api jananam"
english: Birth again, and death again,
and again to lie in a mother's womb.

source: Bhaja Govindam, verse beginning "punar api jananam" (continued)
english: This round of worlds is hard to cross:
in your boundless mercy, save me, Murari!
note: Sung as "khalu dustare"; many editions read "bahu-dustare".

english: Worship Govinda, worship Govinda,
worship Govinda, O foolish mind!

source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship (first half)
english: As rain fallen from the sky
makes its way to the sea...
note: Sung with "sagaram pratigacchati", as heard; the usual text reads "yatha gacchati sagaram".

speaker: Shankara
english: Who would delight in a life too long?
note: Said to Death, who has come as a boy; only the quotation is given here.

speaker: Shankara
english: Brahman alone am I; and all this world
is but an outspreading of pure Consciousness.

speaker: Shankara
english: And all of it, without remainder, is conjured by me
through the three-stranded power of ignorance.

speaker: Shankara
english: He whose conviction stands firm in that
utterly blissful, eternal, supreme, stainless Reality,

speaker: Shankara
english: be he an outcaste, be he a Brahmin, is my Guru:
this is my firm conviction.

speaker: Shankara
source: Kashi Panchakam (attributed to Shankara), verse beginning "kashyam hi kashate kashi"
english: Kashi shines out within Kashi:
Kashi is the light that illumines all.
note: Kashi is named from "kash", to shine: the hymn identifies the holy city with consciousness itself.

speaker: Shankara
source: Kashi Panchakam, verse beginning "kashyam hi kashate kashi" (continued)
english: Whoever has known that Kashi
has truly arrived in Kashi.
Only the clay is real.

speaker: Shankara
english: The water in the eye is the god of rain,
the pupil is the sun;
note: The passage begins earlier, with Rudra in the red lines of the eye, which is not clearly audible.

speaker: Shankara
english: its black is fire, its white is Indra,
and through the lower eyelid, the earth attends it.

speaker: Hastamalaka
english: The One that runs through all things,
yet is touched by none of them,
note: The boy thought to be mute answers Shankara with this verse; Shankara names him Hastamalaka, "amalaka fruit in the hand".

speaker: Hastamalaka
english: ever pure and clear like the sky:
I am that Self, whose nature is eternal awareness.

speaker: Shankara
english: What is night for all beings,
in that the one who is restrained is awake.

speaker: Shankara
english: Passing to another body, the self goes enveloped:
so the question and the answer show.

speaker: Shankara
source: Shankara's commentary on the Brahma Sutras, on 3.1.1
english: It is understood that the soul leaves its former body
and passes into another.
note: The debate follows the wording of Shankara's own commentary closely; only those passages are given here.

speaker: Shankara
source: Shankara's commentary on the Brahma Sutras, on 3.1.1
english: The question is whether it goes
wrapped in the subtle elements, or not.
note: The commentary has "deha-bijair" before "bhuta-sukshmaih" and puts the two alternatives the other way round; the film's wording is slightly simplified.

speaker: Shankara
source: Shankara's commentary on the Brahma Sutras, on 3.1.1
english: "Passing to another" means to another body:
it goes forth wrapped in the subtle elements.

speaker: Shankara
source: Shankara's commentary on the Brahma Sutras, on 3.1.1
english: How do we know? From the question and the answer.

speaker: Shankara
source: Shankara's commentary on the Brahma Sutras, on 3.1.1, quoting Chandogya Upanishad 5.3.3
devanagari: तथा हि प्रश्नः — वेत्थ यथा पञ्चम्याम्
iast: tathā hi praśnaḥ — vettha yathā pañcamyām
english: The question is: "Do you know how, at the fifth offering,
the waters come to be called man?"

speaker: Shankara
source: Shankara's commentary on the Brahma Sutras, on 3.1.1, quoting Chandogya Upanishad 5.9.1
devanagari: निरूपणं च प्रतिवचनं च — इति तु पञ्चम्याम्
iast: nirūpaṇaṃ ca prativacanaṃ ca — iti tu pañcamyām
english: And the answer that explains it:
"Thus at the fifth offering the waters are called man."

speaker: Shankara
english: But water is threefold,
and named for what predominates in it.
That world is a fire, Gautama:
the sun is its fuel, the rays its smoke,
the day its flame, the moon its embers,
the stars its sparks.
Into this fire the gods offer faith;
from that offering King Soma is born.
The rain-cloud is a fire, Gautama:
the wind its fuel, the mist its smoke,
lightning its flame, the thunderbolt its embers,
the rolling thunder its sparks.
Into this fire the gods offer King Soma;
from that offering rain is born.
The earth is a fire, Gautama:
the year its fuel, the sky its smoke,
note: Recognition heard "purusho" here, but the text is "prthivi" (earth), as the feminine "tasyah" that follows confirms.

english: the night its flame, the four quarters its embers,
the points between them its sparks.
Into this fire the gods offer rain;
from that offering food is born.
Man is a fire, Gautama:
speech its fuel, breath its smoke,
the tongue its flame, the eyes its embers,
the ears its sparks.
Into this fire the gods offer food;
from that offering seed is born.

devanagari: तस्या उपस्थ एव समिद्यदुपमन्त्रयते स धूमः
iast: tasyā upastha eva samidyadupamantrayate sa dhūmaḥ
english: Woman is a fire, Gautama:
her loins the fuel, the invitation the smoke,
the womb the flame, union the embers,
its pleasures the sparks.
Into this fire the gods offer seed;
from that offering the child in the womb is born.
So it is that, at the fifth offering,
the waters come to be called man.

devanagari: स उल्बावृतो गर्भो दश वा नव वा
iast: sa ulbāvṛto garbho daśa vā nava vā
english: Wrapped in the caul, the child lies within for ten months,
or nine, or however long, and then is born.
Once born, he lives out his allotted span.
When he has died, they carry him to the fire,
back to where he came from, where he was born.

source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship (opening words)
english: As rain fallen from the sky...

source: Traditional prayer to the Narmada, said for protection from snakes
devanagari: नमोऽस्तु नर्मदे तुभ्यं त्राहि मां विषसर्पतः॥
iast: namo'stu narmade tubhyaṃ trāhi māṃ viṣasarpataḥ ||
english: Homage to the Narmada at dawn and at night;
homage to you, Narmada: guard me from serpents' venom.
note: Often attributed to the Vishnu Purana; we have not been able to confirm this.

source: Hymn to Mitra (Rigveda 3.59.6, in a variant reading)
english: The glory of Mitra, the god who upholds all peoples,
is true, all-winning, and of the brightest renown.

source: Hymn to Mitra (Rigveda 3.59.1, in a variant reading), opening words
english: Mitra, knowing all, sets the peoples in order...

speaker: Mandana Mishra
source: Vedic injunction, often cited in Mimamsa (quoted)
english: As long as he lives, he offers the Agnihotra.
note: Mandana cites it to argue that ritual action is a lifelong duty. Exact source to be confirmed.

speaker: Shankara
english: Knowing Him thus, one becomes immortal here and now:
there is no other way...
note: Quoted only as far as "nanyah pantha". A similar line is in the Shvetashvatara Upanishad, 3.8.

speaker: Ubhaya Bharati
english: That from which words turn back...
note: Only the quotation is given here.

english: As flowing rivers vanish into the ocean,
leaving behind their names and forms,
so the knower, freed from name and form,
reaches the divine Person, beyond the beyond.

speaker: Shankara
source: Nirvana Shatkam (Atma Shatkam), verse 4 (attributed to Shankara)
devanagari: न पुण्यं न पापं न सौख्यं न दुःखं
न मन्त्रो न तीर्थं न वेदा न यज्ञाः।
iast: na puṇyaṃ na pāpaṃ na saukhyaṃ na duḥkhaṃ
na mantro na tīrthaṃ na vedā na yajñāḥ |
english: No merit, no sin; no pleasure, no pain;
no mantra, no pilgrimage, no Vedas, no sacrifice.

speaker: Shankara
devanagari: अहं भोजनं नैव भोज्यं न भोक्ता
iast: ahaṃ bhojanaṃ naiva bhojyaṃ na bhoktā
english: Not the eating, not the food, not the one who eats:
I am consciousness and bliss. I am Shiva, I am Shiva.

source: Prapanchasara Tantra, opening verse, in praise of Sharada (attributed to Shankara)
english: Whose face, arms, feet, waist and eyes are made
of the seven groups of letters, from a to ya:
note: Editions differ in the second line; ours follows the audio ("madhyakshirupa").

english: ruler of all the worlds, eternal, the source of all:
may Sharada grant your minds their purity.

devanagari: सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वाः
iast: sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvāḥ
english: Seven are your fuel-sticks, Agni, seven your tongues,
seven your seers, seven your beloved abodes;
note: Recovered from the pass with the voice filter off; heavily garbled but unmistakable. The Samhita ends the verse with "svaha", which is not clearly audible here.

english: seven priests worship you in seven ways:
fill your seven sources with ghee.

source: Annapurna Stotram (attributed to Shankara), verse beginning "nityanandakari"
english: Ever-joyful, granting boons and fearlessness,
sea of beauty, great Goddess who washes sin away,
note: Readings follow the audio where editions differ. Every line has been checked against the metre (shardulavikridita).

english: purifier of the Himalaya's royal line:
Queen of Kashi, gracious Annapurna, give me alms!
Womb of the universe, bearer of all its glories,
who plays out the drama of the world, flame of wisdom,
you who gladden the heart of Vishvanatha:
Queen of Kashi, gracious Annapurna, give me alms!
Bliss of yoga, slayer of foes, upholder of dharma,
bright as sun, moon and fire, guarding the three worlds,
giver of all power, and of the fruit of penance:
Queen of Kashi, gracious Annapurna, give me alms!
Goddess bright with every jewel, Dakshayani, the fair,
gracious, nourishing, loving, goddess of good fortune,
granting the devotee's wish, ever bringing good:
Queen of Kashi, gracious Annapurna, give me alms!
Queen of the earth and all its peoples, sea of mercy,
her hair dark as a braid of blue, giver of daily food,
giver of liberation itself, ever bringing good:
Queen of Kashi, gracious Annapurna, give me alms!

speaker: Shankara
english: My homeland is the three worlds.
note: Shankara's answer when asked where he will live; only the quotation is given here.

source: Vedasara Shiva Stava (attributed to Shankara), verse beginning "paratmanam ekam"
english: The supreme Self, the One, the first seed of the world,
free of desire, formless, known through Om:
note: The same verse as at 0:08:03, now sung in full.

source: Vedasara Shiva Stava, verse beginning "paratmanam ekam" (continued)
english: from whom the world is born, by whom it is sustained,
I worship that Lord, in whom the world dissolves.

speaker: Shankara
english: For those who walk the path beyond the three gunas,
what is enjoined, and what forbidden?
note: Shankara's answer when told that scripture forbids a monk to perform his mother's funeral rites. A widely quoted line; its source is to be confirmed.

english: No mother, no father,
no kinsman, no brother;
note: A well-known traditional verse; its source is to be confirmed. The first words are not clearly audible.

english: no wealth, no home:
so wake up, wake up!
So wake up, wake up!
Other gods raise a hand to grant boons and safety;
you alone make no such sign,

devanagari: शरण्ये लोकानां तव हि चरणावेव निपुणौ॥
iast: śaraṇye lokānāṃ tava hi caraṇāveva nipuṇau ||
english: for to save from fear, and give more than is wished,
your feet alone suffice, refuge of the worlds.
Breath, truly, is the gatherer.
note: From the story of Raikva and King Janashruti; only the Upanishad's words are given here.

devanagari: प्राणं श्रोत्रं प्राणं मनः। प्राणो ह्येवैतान्सर्वान्संवृङ्क्ते॥
iast: prāṇaṃ śrotraṃ prāṇaṃ manaḥ | prāṇo hyevaitānsarvānsaṃvṛṅkte ||
english: Speech goes into breath, and the eye, the ear, the mind:
breath gathers all of them into itself.
I am Brahman.
note: Thrown back at Shankara mockingly by a Kapalika who wants to sacrifice him; only the quotation is given here.

speaker: Shankara
english: Let my chatter be prayer, every gesture a mudra,
my walking a circling of you, my eating an offering,
note: Shankara's prayer as he offers his body to the Kapalika.

speaker: Shankara
english: my lying down a prostration, all my joys self-giving:
may all that I do become your worship.
Your brow, shining with the pure light of beauty,
seems a second crescent, beside the one in your crown;
set together the other way round, the two would join,
sealed with nectar, into the full moon.
Mountain-born mother, the milk from your heart
is an ocean, I think, of Sarasvati's eloquence;
tasting what you gave in mercy, the Dravida child
became a poet, beloved among the great poets.
note: Tradition reads the "Dravida child" as the Tamil saint Jnanasambandar, or as Shankara himself.

speaker: Shankara
english: Arise! Awake!
note: Only the quotation is given here.

english: Passing beyond this self made of breath...
note: Recognition looped on this one phrase. The chant probably passes through all five "selves" (food, breath, mind, understanding, bliss) and may begin well before this. Needs a careful listen.

english: Only by the grace of God
does the longing for non-duality arise in a person.
note: The film follows it with a line of its own, which is not given here.

speaker: Shankara
english: Joined to a purified understanding,
mastering himself with steadiness,
note: The film strings together verses 18.51, 18.49 and 18.53.

speaker: Shankara
english: letting go of sound and the other objects of sense,
casting off attraction and aversion,

speaker: Shankara
english: Unattached in mind, self-mastered, free of longing,
he reaches, through renunciation, perfect actionlessness.

speaker: Shankara
devanagari: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्।
iast: ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham |
english: Free of ego, force, pride, desire, anger and grasping,
selfless and at peace, he is fit to become Brahman.

source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship (first half)
english: As rain fallen from the sky
makes its way to the sea...
note: The film ends as it began. Sung with "sagaram pratigacchati", as heard.

source: Traditional verse, recited at the close of daily worship (first half, repeated)
english: As rain fallen from the sky
makes its way to the sea...

source: Peace invocation of the Isha Upanishad (also Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 5.1.1)
english: That is whole; this is whole;
from the whole, the whole comes forth.

source: Peace invocation of the Isha Upanishad (continued)
english: Take the whole from the whole,
and the whole alone remains.
